headline: Google's €13bn Finnish bet powers AI while saving nuclear plant
meta_description: Google announces its largest European investment—€13bn in Finland for AI data centres, backed by a 22-year nuclear power deal that will support over 37,000 job…
summary_short: Google invests €13bn in Finland for AI infrastructure, securing half the output of the Loviisa nuclear plant in a 22-year deal that signals confidence in the country's c…
body:
Google will pour €13 billion into Finland's AI infrastructure in what amounts to the company's single largest investment anywhere in Europe, anchored by an unusual commitment: buying up to half the electricity from one of the country's nuclear power plants. The deal, announced this week, pairs three new data centres with an expansion of Google's existing facility in Hamina—a converted paper mill from 2009—plus dedicated funding for clean energy projects and local community initiatives. But the real story lies in what makes the deal work: a 22-year contract with Finnish utility Fortum to draw power from the Loviisa nuclear station, which currently generates about one-tenth of Finland's total electricity.

The arrangement solves a problem both parties face. Google needs reliable, low-carbon energy to fuel the vast computing demands of AI services like its Gemini chatbot, while Fortum gains the financial certainty to extend the Loviisa plant's operating life and boost its capacity. Construction of the new sites in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala will begin in 2027 and 2028, expected to support more than 37,000 jobs during that phase and add €3.6 billion annually to Finland's GDP.

Finland's appeal is straightforward: a cool climate that reduces server cooling costs, abundant renewable and nuclear electricity, and a skilled tech workforce. The timing matters too. This week alone, TikTok announced a separate $1 billion Finnish data centre investment, reflecting how technology companies are racing to secure power supplies as AI demand surges. For Finland, these commitments represent validation of its long-term strategy—and proof that building AI infrastructure responsibly, with clean energy and community support at its core, attracts the world's largest companies.
quick_facts: Google's largest single European investment: €13 billion
22-year nuclear power contract: up to 50% of Loviisa plant output
Three new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala
€3.6 billion annual boost to Finland's GDP from the deal
